name: Saddleback Butte State Park
note: High-desert state park 17 mi E of Lancaster in the Antelope Valley at the base of Saddleback Butte (Joshua-tree woodland). Campground off 170th St E between Ave J and Ave K: ~37 developed sites (~50 primitive total) with shade ramadas, tables, fire rings, potable water, flush toilets and an RV dump station; no hookups. RVs to ~30 ft; FCFS with some sites reservable. --Claude

name: Woodson Bridge State Recreation Area
note: California SRA on the east bank of the Sacramento River 6 mi east of Corning, in a valley-oak riparian forest. 37 sites (RV-friendly to ~31 ft, plus tent-only and a group site); no hookups; flush toilets, hot showers, drinking water. Reservable via ReserveCalifornia, FCFS off-peak. --Claude

name: Baker Creek Campground
note: Inyo County campground in a meadow along Baker Creek just west of Big Pine (Eastern Sierra, off US-395). ~40 sites, no hookups, vault toilets, no showers. Sites vary - some fit 30-ft rigs, others small/unlevel, so pick a larger site for a 23-ft rig. Mix of FCFS and reservable. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Big Lagoon County Park
note: Humboldt County park on the sand spit between the Pacific and Big Lagoon, 7 mi N of Trinidad. 25 sites for tents and small-to-mid RVs/trailers (not all sites fit larger rigs), flush toilets, coin showers, potable water, boat launch. First-come, first-served, 7-night max, on-site host. --Claude

name: Cache Creek Regional Park
note: Yolo County park (Middle Site) on a bend of Cache Creek ~6 mi N of Rumsey on Hwy 16. 45 individual sites (plus group sites); sites 30-45 cap at 26 ft, others vary. Restrooms, showers, turf areas. ~2/3 reservable (48 hr ahead), rest first-come first-served. --Claude

name: Frogtown RV Park (Calaveras County Fairgrounds)
note: Year-round public RV park on the Calaveras County Fairgrounds (Frogtown), 2465 Gun Club Rd, Angels Camp. 68 sites incl full-hookup and pond sites, 60-ft pull-throughs, tent sites; open 24 hrs, self-service check-in. First-come, first-served except reservations for fair events (Jumping Frog Jubilee). County-fair-run. --Claude

name: Calico Ghost Town Campground
note: San Bernardino County Regional Park campground below the historic Calico ghost town, Yermo. ~250+ sites for RVs/trailers/tents: 60+ full-hookup (30/50-amp), many W/E and no-hookup, pull-throughs; hot showers, restrooms, two dump stations. 14-day max stay; reservable for events, otherwise FCFS. County-operated. --Claude

name: Choinumni Park
note: Fresno County park on the Kings River near Piedra, ~3 mi below Pine Flat Dam. 75 riverside sites accommodating RVs/trailers/tents (no hookups) plus a group area. Single sites are first-come, first-served (group by phone). Undergoing a Prop-68 renovation (2022+) with limited sites during construction -- confirm availability before arrival. County-operated. --Claude

name: Clam Beach County Park
note: Humboldt County beach park off Hwy 101, ~7.5 mi N of Arcata near McKinleyville. ~13-18 primitive sites (incl large pull-throughs for RVs), first-come first-served, 3-night max, cash/check; vault toilets, running water, no showers. Sites sit behind the beach dunes. County-operated. --Claude

name: El Dorado County Fairgrounds RV Park
note: Year-round RV area at the El Dorado County Fairgrounds (Fair & Event Center) in Placerville off Hwy 50; 20 full-hookup pull-through sites (30/50/20-amp, water, sewer, dump), showers/laundry, rigs to 50 ft, FCFS plus online reservations. Gated facility closes around large fair events. --Claude

name: Laguna Seca Recreation Area
note: Monterey County recreation area surrounding WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca between Salinas and Monterey; hillside/paddock campground with tent and RV sites, some full-hookup, reservable (fills on race weekends). RV Life ~96 sites, 4*/$$$ (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Lost Lake Recreation Area
note: Fresno County park along the San Joaquin River below Friant Dam. ~42 drive-in sites in the riverside cottonwood corridor, some with hookups; reservable. RV Life 5*/$$ (few reviews). --Claude

name: OC Fair & Event Center RV Camping
note: On-site RV camping at the OC Fair & Event Center (32nd DAA) in Costa Mesa; full-hookup pull-through/back-in sites (20-amp elec, water, sewer) in a paved lot with dump station, first-come-first-served, 14-day max stay. Open to the public outside scheduled event/fair closures (closed roughly Apr, mid-May, Jun-Aug OC Fair, and mid-Sep-early Oct). --Claude

name: Rocky Point Campground (Lake Almanor)
note: PG&E-operated campground on the wooded west shore of Lake Almanor (Rocky Point peninsula near Canyon Dam); ~130 drive-in forest sites, no hookups, sandy beach/day-use nearby. Utility-run, so classed private per convention. Verify current reservation channel (PG&E recreation / recreation.gov) vs FCFS with the operator. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Ponderosa Flat Campground (Butt Valley Reservoir)
note: PG&E utility-operated campground on the east shore of Butt Valley Reservoir (Butt Lake) near Canyondam; ~63 drive-in sites, vault toilets, boat ramp and swim beach, no hookups. First-come, first-served. Utility recreation land = private by convention. --Claude  Road work on Butt-Prattville Road near Cool Springs, Ray Adams Boat Launch and Ponderosa Flat from Aug 10, 2026 through the rest of the 2026 season: traffic delays, heavy trucks, noise and dust (PG&E notice, 2026-10-10). --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Steckel Park
note: Ventura County park along Santa Paula Creek on Hwy 150 NE of Santa Paula. Drive-in tent/RV campground (upper and lower loops) in an oak/creek setting; some sites have water/electric hookups. Reservable via Ventura County Parks. RV Life 4*/$$$, review as recent as 8/2025 (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Taboose Creek Campground
note: Inyo County campground on Taboose Creek in the Owens Valley, ~14 mi N of Independence at the base of the Sierra. ~35-50 primitive drive-in sites, big rigs OK (RVs to ~36 ft), no hookups, potable water well, vault toilets, stream access. Mix of FCFS and reservable (ReserveAmerica). --Claude

name: Tapo Canyon Park
note: County/park-district park in Tapo Canyon N of Simi Valley (Rancho Simi Recreation & Park District area). Drive-in campground with picnic areas, horseback-riding facilities, and ~16 RV hookup sites (a general campground that also offers equestrian use, not horse-only). RV Life 4.5*/$$$, 58 reviews with one as recent as 8/2025 confirming current operation (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Tehachapi Mountain Park
note: Kern County mountain park at ~5800 ft on the flank of Tehachapi Mountain; forested campsites with tables, fire rings, potable water and vault toilets, no hookups. First-come, first-served (cash at entrance). Access via a steep, narrow, winding road (posted 28-ft vehicle max); firsthand reviews say the campground loops are tight/curvy and best for smaller-to-moderate rigs, so a 23-ft rig can access but expect a slow, careful drive. --Claude

name: Trinity County Fairgrounds RV Camping
note: RV camping at the Trinity County Fairgrounds in Hayfork (mountain valley off CA-3). Fairgrounds RV sites with hookups available for rent through the fairgrounds office; large open grounds. Thinly reviewed (RV Life 1 review). Contact the fairgrounds to confirm availability outside fair week. --Claude

name: Veterans Memorial Park Campground
note: City of Monterey-run Veterans Memorial Park campground in the wooded hills above downtown Monterey. ~40 drive-in sites, first-come first-served, dry camping (no hookups), RVs accommodated with a short stay limit. --Claude

name: Wiest Lake County Park
note: Imperial County-run lakeside park on Wiest Lake (fed by the Alamo River) north of Brawley, ~150 ft below sea level. Drive-in RV sites with hookups, boat launch and fishing; renovated and reopened in recent years. Thinly reviewed (RV Life 1 rating). Satellite confirms a developed shoreline park with drive-in access. --Claude

name: Woodward Reservoir Regional Park
note: Stanislaus County regional park on Woodward Reservoir (operated with South San Joaquin Irrigation District). RV/trailer hookup camping across six areas (T-Island, Hackberry Flat, Mountain View Point, Fischer Point, Muir Point, Charlie's Point) plus first-come-first-served basic sites; hookup sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Mill Valley Campground
note: Small forest campground ~17 mi west of Stonyford, ~1 mi from Letts Lake in Mendocino NF (Grindstone RD). 15 sites for trailers to ~24 ft (one source lists 32 ft), tables/fire rings, no potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (pay on-site). Burned in the 2020 August Complex. --Claude

name: Letts Lake Campground
note: On 35-acre Letts Lake ~19 mi west of Stonyford in Mendocino NF (Grindstone RD). 42 sites across 4 loops (Main Letts, Saddle Camp, Spillway, Stirrup); access and sites suit trailers to ~30 ft (some 35-ft rigs reported). Vault toilets, seasonal water, no hookups; non-motorized boating/trout fishing. First-come, first-served (pay on-site QR). Area burned in the 2020 August Complex. --Claude

name: Navy Camp (Lake Pillsbury)
note: PG&E-operated Lake Pillsbury campground in Mendocino NF; single loop of ~20 sites with paved parking aprons under valley oaks, vault toilets, no hookups; posted vehicle max ~22 ft (pads ~12x25 ft, borderline for a 23-ft rig). First-come, first-served, open ~May-Sept. Lake Pillsbury reservoir and its recreation facilities are slated for removal under PG&E's Potter Valley Project decommissioning (dam removal proposed ~2028+); currently operating. --Claude  All sites first-come, first-served; no reservations (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Fuller Grove Campground (Lake Pillsbury)
note: PG&E-operated campground on the west shore of Lake Pillsbury (Mendocino NF); ~23 individual sites (incl. six doubles) plus a reservable group site, paved aprons (the more RV-friendly of the Pillsbury camps), boat ramp and beach access, vault toilets, no hookups. Individual sites first-come, first-served (group site reservable online); open ~May-Sept. Reservoir/facilities slated for removal under PG&E's Potter Valley Project decommissioning; currently operating. --Claude  All sites first-come, first-served; no reservations (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Oak Flat Campground (Lake Pillsbury)
note: PG&E-operated Lake Pillsbury campground (Mendocino NF); ~12 primitive sites with a dispersed feel among valley oaks on the NW shore, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups; interior access is rough dirt, best for shorter/self-contained rigs. Open year-round. Reservoir/facilities slated for removal under PG&E's Potter Valley Project decommissioning; currently operating. --Claude All sites first-come, first-served; no reservations (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Mill Creek Campground (Mendocino NF)
note: Small USFS roadside campground in Mendocino NF, ~8 mi west of Stonyford on Rd 18N01 along Mill Creek (South Fork Stony Creek); 6 sites with tables and fire rings, vault toilet, no hookups. First-come, first-served with Recreation.gov scan-and-pay. --Claude

name: South Fork Campground (Mendocino NF)
note: USFS campground in Mendocino NF ~9.5 mi west of Stonyford on Rd 18N03 at the South Fork Stony Creek; two camping areas, ~10 sites, tables and fire rings, vault toilet, no hookups; accommodates trailers up to ~30 ft. First-come, first-served with Recreation.gov scan-and-pay. --Claude

name: Plaskett Meadows Campground
note: USFS campground in Mendocino NF on Forest Hwy 7 (~6,050 ft), reopened June 2026; ~31 sites for trailers/RVs to 26 ft in mixed pine and fir beside two small trout lakes (Plaskett Lakes), potable water (as of 2026), vault toilets, no hookups; interior road is dirt and tight. First-come, first-served with Recreation.gov scan-and-pay. --Claude

name: Mad River Campground (Six Rivers NF)
note: USFS campground in Six Rivers NF on a bluff overlooking the Mad River, ~2 mi south of Ruth Lake; 40 single-family sites for tents and RVs (sites vary, many to ~26-35 ft), vault toilets, no hookups; the majority of sites are adjacent to the river. Reservable on Recreation.gov with some sites first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Pigeon Point Campground
note: Small Shasta-Trinity NF campground on the Wild & Scenic Trinity River off Hwy 299, ~15 mi W of Weaverville. 7 single-family sites (plus a separately reservable group site), picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, no potable water; small rigs only, max RV ~22 ft. Single sites first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Nordheimer Campground
note: Six Rivers NF campground on the Salmon (Wild & Scenic) River near Forks of Salmon; ~12 family sites (first-come, first-served, fee area) plus 4 reservable group sites, vault toilets, no drinking water. The Salmon River Rd narrows to one lane with tight corners and cliffs past Butler Creek so larger rigs are discouraged, but it is a normal-vehicle (not 4WD) drive and the riverside flat fits a mid-size rig. --Claude

name: Sarah Totten Campground
note: Klamath NF campground shaded next to the Klamath (Wild & Scenic) River ~1 mi east of the historic Hamburg townsite; 9 family sites (first-come, first-served) plus 2 reservable group sites, accommodates tents, trailers and RVs, vault toilets, drinking water, sandy boat launch for drift boats/rafters. --Claude

name: Lower Salt Creek Shoreline Area
note: Drive-in dispersed shoreline camping area on the Sacramento arm of Shasta Lake off Lower Salt Creek Rd (Shasta-Trinity NF); no designated sites, portable toilet and boat launch, first-come first-served (pack-in/pack-out, no facilities off-season). --Claude

name: McCloud Bridge Campground
note: Shasta-Trinity NF campground on the McCloud arm of Shasta Lake, ~17 mi in on Gilman Rd; 14 sites (11 single, 3 double), vault toilets, no hookups; RVs to ~35 ft, first-come first-served. --Claude

name: Hawkins Landing Campground
note: PG&E-operated (utility) campground on the forested shore of Iron Canyon Reservoir near Big Bend; ~10 paved sites, most level and long enough for a 24-ft trailer (no hookups), boat ramp and sandy beach; Access is a rough, pothole-heavy gravel road from Big Bend - passable but hard on trailers. --Claude All sites first-come, first-served; no reservations (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Lava Beds National Monument - Indian Well Campground
note: Lava Beds NM's only developed campground; 43 individual sites first-come, first-served plus one reservable group site, flush toilets and drinking water, no hookups. Motorhomes up to 30 ft (not all sites fit large rigs). --Claude

name: Shafter Campground
note: Klamath NF (Goosenest RD) campground in Butte Valley beside trout-stocked Butte Creek; ~10 sites, vault toilets, no potable water, dump available, first-come, first-served, RVs to about 40 ft. Open May-Oct. --Claude
